title: Nimbus: admin playlet simulator & telemetry-aware fallthroughs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
Support engineers currently validate runbook changes by running ad-hoc scripts or staging flows that do not reflect production telemetry and fallthrough behavior. This leads to regressions where automated playbook steps (playlets) succeed in dry runs but cause unexpected side-effects when routed through runtime fallbacks or when observability sampling is enabled.

Goal:
Build a repeatable "playlet simulator" (Nimbus) that executes runbooks-as-tasks in a controlled dryrun mode while replaying production-like telemetry and routing fallthrough scenarios. Simulator should be pluggable into CI, available in the admin console sandbox, and produce deterministic diffs against a golden baseline.

Scope:
- Simulator runs at step-level granularity (invoke a single playlet or a chain).
- Replays telemetry signals (latency spikes, partial failures, kv-cache cold hits) from synthetic traces or sampled production traces.
- Emulates smart-routing fallthroughs (model variant fallbacks, region failover, capacity-tier switch).
- Generates an actionable report: step outcomes, telemetry timeline, provenance links, suggested mitigations.
- Integrates with telemetry infra to annotate spans and to push synthetic events to the same observability pipeline used in staging (not production).

Out of scope for initial PRD:
- Full UI for creating playlets (we will use existing playlet editor).
- Auto-remediation/one-click rollouts (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can run a playlet chain in dryrun mode and produce a step-by-step log identical across repeated runs given same trace seed
Simulator replays a supplied trace (format: line-delimited JSON events) and injects synthetic latency/failure at configured points
Simulator exposes an API endpoint for CI to request a dryrun and returns a structured report link
Report includes: step status, telemetry timeline, routing decisions, link to related GitHub PR if provided
Telemetry replay runs against the staging observability pipeline and is throttled to avoid alert noise in production

decisions: Use a seedable synthetic trace format (line-delimited JSON events) as primary replay input to avoid PII exposure from sampled production traces
Telemetry integration will be read-only and write to a dedicated staging dataset to prevent alerting in prod
Determinism guarantee documented: simulator only guarantees identical outputs when both playlet code and trace seed are unchanged
Expose the simulator as an internal HTTP service (nimbus-sim) and a lightweight CLI shim for engineers
next_steps: Wire up the staging observability credentials and create a sandbox org for simulator traffic (ENG infra task)
Complete PR: initial simulator runner and trace seeding support (link in attachments)
Add acceptance tests in CI: run simulator against three canonical playlets and assert report schema
Schedule a design pass with Console team to show proof-of-concept report (target: 2025-W09)
Coordinate with Security to sign off on trace handling and retention (security_review_required=true)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Replay of production traces could leak sensitive info. Mitigation: only allow sanitized sample export and prefer synthetic seeds for day-to-day testing
Risk: Simulator could generate noisy telemetry. Mitigation: route to staging dataset with rate-limiting and a kill switch controlled by ops
Risk: Drift between simulator behavior and prod runtime kernels (quantization/speed). Mitigation: add a version tag in report and include runtime kernel profile snapshot for comparison
